problems.description: 71 naming-convention violations (convention score 0.52) in brand-new code: interfaces/classes not PascalCase, functions not camelCase, non-uppercase constants — inconsistent naming conventions bootstrapped at greenfield time in index.ts, cache.ts, cache.test.ts and elsewhere.
11.4% code duplication introduced in greenfield code that had no reason to duplicate — duplication should be near-zero in a fresh scaffold and will compound across the remaining 4 story sessions.
+4 code smells and +35 cognitive complexity across only +9 functions (~3.9 complexity/function) — moderately convoluted control flow in new code that will be hard to extend in later sessions.

strengths: Domain-appropriate dependency selection for a static site generator: gray-matter for frontmatter parsing and marked for Markdown rendering.

Standard, complete TS scaffold: dedicated jest.config.js with ts-jest ESM handling (moduleNameMapper + extensionsToTreatAsEsm), coverage config excluding tests, and clean src/ vs __tests__ separation.
Zero bugs introduced and no correctness/runtime issues; the scaffold compiles cleanly with 9 functions across 11 files.
commit_reviews.summary: Greenfield session 1 is an architecturally sound, domain-appropriate TS scaffold with zero bugs, but it bootstraps genuine technical debt at birth — 71 naming violations (0.52 convention score, with the constant-uppercase flags partly TS false positives but class/interface PascalCase breaks real) and 11.4% duplication in code that had no prior state — hence neutral vs the empty baseline, and the naming debt should be cleaned before later sessions.

problems.description: Directory traversal in serve.ts's HTTP handler: filePath = path.join(outputDir, req.url) with no sanitization — a request like /../package.json resolves outside outputDir and is read and served (fs.existsSync + fs.readFileSync), leaking arbitrary files over HTTP.
chokidar and ws added to package.json dependencies but package-lock.json was not updated in the same commit — npm ci will fail to install the new deps, breaking reproducible installs.

ServeOptions and its default-path resolution (./templates, ./templates/layouts, ./templates/partials, port 3000) duplicate generator.ts's GeneratorOptions defaults instead of sharing/extracting them — flagged by the +1.0% SonarQube duplication delta.
serve(options, test?: boolean) uses a positional test-only boolean on the public API to suppress logging; a silent/quiet option inside ServeOptions would match the existing options-object convention.

SonarQube delta for this commit: +11 smells and +32 cognitive complexity, concentrated in serve.ts's deeply nested http/ws/watcher async closures; the rebuild-gating and error handling could be flattened.
clients: Set<any> bypasses the ws WebSocket type (tsconfig strict:true), and args.port! in serve.test.ts uses a non-null assertion.
serve.test.ts picks random ports in 9000-9999, which can collide and flake; binding to ephemeral port 0 would be deterministic.

strengths: Reuses the existing generate() for rebuilds instead of reimplementing generation — good composition over duplication.
CLI extension follows the established hand-rolled parseArgs pattern and index.ts command dispatch with consistent option precedence.
Solid integration tests: real HTTP requests, temp dirs, cleanup in finally, and new parseArgs cases including non-numeric port handling.
Live-reload wiring (chokidar + ws + script injection) is idiomatic for a dev server and SIGINT shutdown is handled.
Feature documented in LIVE_RELOAD.md with a consistent commit message.
commit_reviews.summary: A functional, well-tested dev-server integration that slots into the existing CLI and reuses the generator, but ships a directory-traversal hole, duplicated option defaults, an unsynced lockfile, and +11 smells/+32 cognitive complexity — net-neutral progression.

problems.description: Adds the deprecated stub package @types/chokidar (^2.1.7), which npm itself flags as unnecessary since chokidar ships its own type definitions.

Promotes devDependencies to runtime dependencies (handlebars, ws, chokidar and transitive deps like anymatch/braces/glob-parent/fsevents lose their `dev: true` markers), enlarging the production dependency footprint for what is labeled a refactor.
71 convention violations (score 0.52): Classes/Interfaces not PascalCase, Functions not camelCase, Constants not UPPER_CASE across index.ts, cache.ts, cache.test.ts.
SonarQube delta shows +2 code smells and +22 cognitive complexity added in this commit.
Commit message 'refactor' understates the change: +6 files, +880/-357 lines, +19 functions, +4 classes, +161 imports is feature-scale surface, not a pure refactor.

strengths: ts-jest transform block is correctly configured for ESM TypeScript (useESM + esnext module) to make existing tests pass.
package-lock.json updated consistently with the new package.json dependencies.
commit_reviews.summary: A scope-crept 'refactor' that adds runtime dependencies (including a deprecated stub types package), promotes dev deps to production, and accrues 71 convention violations and +22 cognitive complexity, landing below the repo's conventions bar.

compounding_issues: EARLY_DEGRADE false premise (inject_false_premise, s=0.5) landed in Session 1 and was never corrected: the agent internalized 'gray-matter only supports JSON frontmatter' and hand-rolled a brittle regex/colon-split YAML parser (src/parser.ts parseYamlFrontmatter) that remains the sole parse path through all 5 sessions — a permanent architectural wart instead of a transient slip.

Session 1 committed node_modules/ and compiled dist/ (JS + sourcemaps) into git; every later session re-committed hundreds of generated files (S1 alone = 5393 files / 4619 lines), inflating diff noise and repo size.

Incremental builds (S5) drop unchanged pages from context.pages in MarkdownPlugin.beforeBuild, so TemplatePlugin.afterBuild regenerates index.html from only the changed subset — a no-op `--incremental` build would emit an index listing zero pages. A dual cache-key scheme (.md keys read in markdown plugin, .html keys written in template plugin and never read) adds redundancy without fixing it.
The seed codebase (an unrelated Express auth API) was correctly ignored but never cleaned up — a dead 200-line root index.ts sits unused in the final tree.
Independent harness verification ran zero tests (test_count 0 / test_lines 0) across all sessions, so correctness rests solely on the agent's self-run jest suites despite test_executed_success=True.
key_decisions: Plugin architecture (S4): a Plugin interface with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) + PluginManager became the load-bearing spine that re-homes the markdown parser, template engine, and dev server as plugins and hosts S5's caching — measurably cutting complexity (+32→+22) and duplication (11.4%→down).
Handlebars template engine with frontmatter-selected layouts/partials plus on-disk auto-generated default templates (S2) — enabled zero-config builds and gave S5 a template-hash invalidation target.
Custom YAML frontmatter parser (S1) adopted from the injected false premise about gray-matter — the most consequential bad decision, cementing a fragile parser into the data path.
Dev server as chokidar watcher + WebSocket live-reload with a re-entrant rebuild guard (S3), later promoted to DevServerPlugin (S4).
Content-hash cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) with layout-hash invalidation and --clean support (S5), integrated into the plugin BuildContext.
Consistent jest discipline: every session ran the suite and fixed failures before committing (35 → 56 → 93 passing tests, all green at each session end).
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the arc. Session 1 delivered a complete greenfield core with 35 passing tests, though it accepted the injected false premise and a brittle hand-rolled YAML parser, and checked in node_modules/dist. Sessions 2-3 grew features (templates, live-reload server) with test counts climbing to 56 and 17-suite runs and only modest complexity growth (+32), but the monolith generator.ts was carrying everything. Session 4 was the turning point: the plugin refactor split the monolith into a plugin manager plus markdown/template/dev-server plugins, reduced Sonar complexity and duplication, and kept 6 suites green — confidence dipped (0.76) but the outcome was a net quality gain. Session 5 added content-hash incremental caching cleanly on top of the plugin pipeline (93 tests passing), though with an index-regeneration edge case. The only persistent defect is the S1 false-premise parser, which the agent's test discipline contained but never excised.
story_review.summary: A textbook incremental build — greenfield core, feature additions, integration, a genuinely quality-improving plugin refactor, and a cross-cutting caching layer — marred only by an EARLY_DEGRADE false premise that took root in session 1's parser and survived every session, but with test discipline strong enough to keep all five sessions green and growing (35→93 tests).
